Jordan / Aditya —

I've started populating the questionnaire with the technical details. Highlights and proposed wording for the customer packet below (please review inline items I flagged):

1) SAST
- Tooling: We use a mixed pipeline: open-source linters + commercial static analysis (internal build of Semgrep rules and commercial SCA for dependency scanning).
- Cadence: Push/prod branch scanning on every PR (pre-merge) + weekly full-repo scheduled scans. We generate triage queues and assign to owning engineers.
- False positives: triage rules and signature suppression with review — we keep a 'suppress-and-review' lifespan of 90 days, after which suppression entries must be revalidated.

2) DAST
- Tooling: Authenticated dynamic scans for staging + authenticated smoke scans in canary environments. We run DAST weekly for major services and nightly lightweight scans for public endpoints.
- Remediation: Findings are logged to Jira with severity and SLA tags. Medium/High go to a patch-backlog with 30/14 day SLAs respectively (see SLA table).

3) Penetration tests
- cadence: Annual third-party full-scope pentest (external network + application) + targeted retests after major releases. Last full test: 2026-08-05 (third-party: RedwoodSec) — executive summary attached (redwood-pentest-summary-202608.pdf).
- remediation: All high/critical issues closed within 60 days; most fixed within 30 days. We include risk acceptance logs for any deferred items.

4) Patch SLAs (proposed wording for the packet)
- OS critical/zero-day: 72 hours for mitigation plan, 14 days for full remediation where feasible
- Third-party library critical: 14 days for patch or mitigation (compensating control)
- Non-critical/low: incorporated in normal release cycle (next sprint window; typically 30–90 days)
- Emergency escalation: Security Engineering pager + CISO on-call (contacts provided in separate secure doc)

5) SBOM
- generation: We emit dependency manifests during CI (NPM, pip, Maven) and normalize into a canonical CSV and CycloneDX metadata; builds include provenance (commit, build id). Sample SBOM for the hosted runtime will be redwood-sbom-20260914.csv (attached).

6) Compensating controls
- Runtime monitoring (KV cache integrity checks), anomaly detection for unusual token patterns, WAFs in front of public endpoints, and automated canary rollback for suspicious behavior.

Attachments to include in final packet: redwood-sbom-20260914.csv, redwood-pentest-summary-202608.pdf, sast-report-202608.txt (execs only), dast-scan-summary-202608.pdf, patch-sla-overview.pdf

Notes/asks:
- Jordan — confirm whether Summit requires full findings under NDA or if exec summaries + remediation timelines suffice for initial procurement review.
- Aditya — please confirm the DAST schedule phrasing (we sometimes run authenticated scans as nightly in dedicated staging; want to ensure we don't overpromise for hosted-prod).
